references.text: Isaiah prophesies about Jerusalem's judgment and suffering. Jesus uses the expression 'daughters of Jerusalem' in a context of coming judgment, reflecting the prophets' warnings to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. [ref: Isa 13:6-9|Isaiah 13:6-9]

Hosea prophesies that they should say to the mountains 'Fall on us!' and to the hills 'Hide us!' – these are exactly the words Jesus quotes in the following verses as a reason why the daughters of Jerusalem should weep for themselves. [ref: Hos 10:8|Hosea 10:8]

Jeremiah speaks of wailing women who will lament over Jerusalem's destruction. Jesus urges the women to weep for themselves and their children, similar to Jeremiah's lament over Jerusalem. [ref: Jer 9:17-20|Jeremiah 9:17-20]

Jesus wept over Jerusalem and prophesied about the city's destruction – a direct parallel to the warning here that the daughters of Jerusalem should weep for themselves and their children because of the coming judgment. [ref: Luke 19:41-44|Luke 19:41-44]

Jesus speaks about Jerusalem's destruction and says 'Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days,' which directly connects to the warning to weep for their children. [ref: Luke 21:20-24|Luke 21:20-24]

The continuation of Jesus' words to the daughters of Jerusalem, where he expands on the warning by speaking about blessed childless women and crying out to the mountains, as well as the parable of the green and dry tree. [ref: Luke 23:29-31|Luke 23:29-31]

In the end-times vision, people cry out to the mountains and rocks that they should fall on them – a fulfillment of the words Jesus links to the warning about Jerusalem's judgment. [ref: Rev 6:16-17|Revelation 6:16-17]
The Song of Songs uses the expression 'daughters of Jerusalem' as a form of address, the same address Jesus uses here. [ref: Song 1:5|Song of Solomon 1:5]

Jeremiah urges weeping: 'Let your eyes run with tears ... for the Lord's flock has been taken captive.' Jesus' call to weep for themselves and their children reflects this prophetic tradition of lamentation. [ref: Jer 13:17|Jeremiah 13:17]
